label: Heavy vehicle
title: Heavy vehicle safety
headline: Big vehicles, big blind spots, long stops
intro: Fuel tankers, trucks and buses keep the B1 moving. Learn where their drivers can't see you, and why you should never cut in front of one.

scenes.question: Heavy trucks and buses are about {claim:na.stat.heavy-share} of vehicles registered in Namibia. In {n:2026}, up to mid-September, how many people died in crashes involving heavy vehicles?

art.alt: Top-down view of a multi-lane road. Your white car is in the lane to the left of a long fuel tanker.

lines: You're driving north on a dual carriageway near Okahandja. A fuel tanker is in the lane to your right.
You've been driving beside it for a while. Suddenly its left indicator starts to flash.

scenes.prompt: Move your car to where the tanker driver can see you.

art.alt: Top-down view: the tanker is indicating left and your car is beside it. Drag your car forward or back along your lane.

safe.title: The driver can see you
safe.body: You're well behind the tanker. If you can see the driver's face in their side mirror, they can see you. Hanging back also leaves room if it turns.

ahead.title: Seen, but risky
ahead.body: The driver can see you ahead, but a loaded tanker can't stop quickly if you need to slow down. Dropping back is safer.

inside.title: Still in the blind spot
inside.body: Part of your car is where the driver can't see it. If the tanker turns left now, it could hit you.

scenes.prompt: Tap every road user the truck driver can't see.

art.alt: Top-down view of the tanker with eighteen road users around it: cars, a minibus taxi, motorbikes, bicycles and people walking.

feedback.green: You found every road user in the driver's blind spots.
feedback.orange: Some are right, but not all. The shaded zones show where the driver can't see.
feedback.red: These road users are outside the blind spots. The shaded zones show where the driver can't see.

art.alt: The tanker with four numbered blind-spot zones: left side, right side, in front and behind.

steps.title: Left side: the biggest
steps.body: The driver sits on the right, so the left side hides the most. It can cover more than one lane and run back along the tank. Don't stay there, and never pass a truck on the left as it turns.

steps.title: Right side
steps.body: On the driver's side the blind spot runs back from the cab. When you overtake on the right, do it without lingering beside the truck.

steps.title: Just in front
steps.body: Right in front of a high cab, the driver can't see low cars, children, motorbikes or animals. If you pull in ahead, leave plenty of room.

steps.title: Close behind
steps.body: Tucked in behind the tank, the driver can't see you and you can't see the road ahead. Drop back until you can see the truck's mirrors.

scenes.explain: From the start of {n:2026} to mid-September, {claim:na.stat.heavy-deaths-2026} people died and {claim:na.stat.heavy-injured-2026} were injured in {claim:na.stat.heavy-crashes-2026} crashes involving heavy vehicles.

lines: If you can't see the driver in their mirror, they can't see you.
Don't sit beside a truck. Pass it without lingering, or drop back.
Give turning trucks room. They swing wide and can use more than one lane.

scenes.question: A loaded truck is travelling at {claim:na.law.speed-heavy}, its legal maximum in Namibia. About how many metres does it need to stop on a dry road?

art.alt: A truck with symbols for a highway and a car.

lines: You're driving into Windhoek on a dual carriageway. A loaded truck is in the left lane beside you.
You're both doing the same speed. You need to turn left at the traffic lights ahead.

scenes.prompt: The light ahead turns yellow. What do you do?

art.alt: Top-down view: your car is in the right lane, beside a loaded truck in the left lane, approaching traffic lights with two cars waiting in your lane.

options.label: Move into the left lane, in front of the truck
options.title: Too close to call
options.reason: The truck couldn't stop for you. It would still have been doing about {var:truckKmh} km/h when it reached your car. Never cut in front of a heavy vehicle that's braking.

options.label: Stay in my lane and wait
options.title: Good call
options.reason: You kept out of the space the truck needs to stop. Turn left once it's safe, even if it means going round the block.

scenes.prompt: Compare a car and a loaded truck at the same speed.

art.alt: Two bars showing the distance a car and a loaded truck travel before stopping, with minibus taxis drawn underneath for scale.

states.label: {n:40} km/h
states.caption: At {var:kmh} km/h: a car needs about {var:d0} m, a loaded truck about {var:d1} m. That's about {var:taxis1} minibus taxis nose to tail.

states.label: {n:60} km/h
states.caption: At {var:kmh} km/h: a car needs about {var:d0} m, a loaded truck about {var:d1} m. That's about {var:taxis1} minibus taxis nose to tail.

states.label: {n:80} km/h
states.caption: At {var:kmh} km/h: a car needs about {var:d0} m, a loaded truck about {var:d1} m. That's about {var:taxis1} minibus taxis nose to tail.

scenes.explain: At {claim:na.law.speed-heavy} a loaded truck needs roughly {claim:int.truck.stop80} to stop on a dry road. Its air brakes take a moment to work, and its weight takes a long time to slow. Real distances vary with the load, the brakes and the road.

lines: Never cut in front of a truck, especially near traffic lights or a turn.
A loaded truck needs far more road to stop than your car does.
Keep at least {claim:int.uk.gap} behind a truck, and more in rain or dust.
